behavior: Reopens a configured cache root, scans stored checkpoints, and rebuilds the index so target sequence state can be reused after server restart.
dependencies: C++17 filesystem | llama per-sequence state API | POSIX-style file I/O
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has disk prompt-cache spill, but its owned namespace is deliberately removed on shutdown.
rationale: Add an explicit persistent mode to the existing ROCmFPX cache engine rather than replacing its tested run-scoped mode.
risks: Crash consistency, stale format detection, tenant confidentiality, and restart index integrity.

behavior: Classifies checkpoints by recency and moves them through hot, warm, and cold tiers after turns.
dependencies: turn counter | tier RAM budgets | checkpoint metadata
target_overlap: ROCmFPX currently has RAM plus bounded disk entries, not the same three-tier policy.
rationale: Preserve the policy objective but implement one budgeted cache with explicit residency state, pressure feedback, and testable promotion/demotion.
risks: Source defaults and parent overrides disagree; auto budgeting is not cgroup-aware.

behavior: Stores target-model state, optional draft-model state, and speculative-decoder metadata as one logical checkpoint.
dependencies: target llama_context | optional draft context | speculative decoder state
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already persists target/draft pairs and stateful MTP metadata.
rationale: Unify record metadata and validation with ROCmFPX's existing target/draft/state_spec representation.
risks: Partial component restores must never be treated as a complete hit.

behavior: Reads and writes large state blobs in 64 MiB chunks instead of requiring a single giant host operation.
dependencies: pread/pwrite or platform equivalents | bounded temporary buffers
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has robust file commit handling but can reuse a bounded transfer helper where its serialization path benefits.
rationale: Port the chunk-loop concept behind the target's current I/O abstraction and preserve its fault injection.
risks: Short reads/writes and cancellation paths require tests.

behavior: Can force checkpoint data to stable storage unless no-fsync is selected.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already flushes files and directories in its tested commit path.
rationale: Represent durability as an explicit strict/relaxed policy and retain ROCmFPX's atomic pair commit.
risks: CachyLlama writes directly to final names, so fsync alone does not make metadata publication atomic.

behavior: Rejects state whose model/cache compatibility hash differs from the active context.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already validates state shape and file integrity but needs a stable restart-persistence namespace key.
rationale: Define a versioned fingerprint covering model identity, context layout, KV types, backend-relevant serialization version, and draft/MTP shape.
risks: Under-specified fingerprints can load semantically incompatible state.

behavior: Persists a bounded token prefix with checkpoint metadata for restart-time prefix matching.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX's in-memory disk index already tracks complete prompt token vectors for the current run.
rationale: Persist a compact, versioned token index or manifest in persistent mode; verify candidate tokens against the loaded file before accepting.
risks: A 4096-token metadata prefix cannot prove equality for longer prompts by itself.

behavior: Bounds the number of cold checkpoints and evicts old entries from a cold ring.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already enforces a byte limit and LRU eviction.
rationale: Retain count as a secondary guard only; use byte quotas as the primary policy.
risks: Count-only limits behave poorly across models with very different state sizes.

behavior: Derives tier capacities from reported free RAM and allocates most of the calculated budget to the hot tier.
dependencies: Linux sysinfo or platform memory query | host RAM
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has an explicit RAM cache limit.
rationale: Keep explicit limits authoritative; optional auto mode must use MemAvailable/cgroup limits and reserve headroom for model/runtime pressure.
risks: Current free-RAM calculation can overcommit and is not container-aware.

behavior: Issues read-ahead hints for a likely checkpoint before the restore is required.
dependencies: posix_fadvise or platform equivalent | continuation prediction
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has no documented persistent prefetch layer.
rationale: Add as an optional optimization after correctness and persistence land; measure hit rate and I/O amplification.
risks: Prefetch may evict useful page cache or waste I/O on low-confidence candidates.

behavior: Places explicit-user caches under a user-oriented namespace distinct from anonymous conversation roots.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX's current run directory is process-private, not tenant-addressed.
rationale: Use an authenticated tenant ID and opaque keyed hash in the path; never trust a request field as the authorization boundary.
risks: Path disclosure, user-supplied identity spoofing, and owner-wide file permissions.

behavior: Creates cache directories and state files using conventional shared-readable modes in the component path.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX's existing disk cache uses owner-only namespaces and files.
rationale: Do not import CachyLlama's permission choices; keep ROCmFPX's 0700/0600 posture and add optional encryption for persistent multi-tenant use.
risks: Prompts and hidden reasoning can be secrets.

behavior: Writes checkpoint payloads directly to their final paths and removes them on detected failure.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already uses temporary files, atomic rename, and directory synchronization.
rationale: Keep the target's commit protocol; persistent mode should add a manifest transaction rather than regress to direct publication.
risks: Power loss can leave a final-name partial file.

behavior: Centralizes open, pread, pwrite, fsync, unlink, and advisory behavior.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX supports cross-platform server builds and has its own filesystem code.
rationale: Port only useful abstractions, preserving Windows UTF-8 and fault-injection behavior in the target.
risks: A POSIX-named layer is not sufficient for Windows portability.

behavior: Scans checkpoint files and restores cache metadata when no live process index exists.
dependencies: directory scan | metadata decoder | format version
target_overlap: ROCmFPX current entries exist only in process memory and are deleted on exit.
rationale: Use a checksummed manifest plus orphan reconciliation; bound startup cost and quarantine malformed entries.
risks: Unbounded directory scans and corrupted metadata can delay startup.

behavior: Stores a system-prefix sequence state independently of a conversation so requests sharing the same system prompt can skip repeated prefill.
dependencies: system boundary detector | sequence-state API | model compatibility hash
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has general prompt-prefix caching but no separately governed persistent system-prefix store.
rationale: Implement as a scoped prefix-cache class in the target engine, keyed by model/template/tenant/system token sequence.
risks: Cross-tenant leakage and false boundary detection are high-impact.

behavior: Scans sys-{hash}.bin entries and restores their state into an in-memory catalog at startup.
dependencies: persistent files | startup scan | RAM catalog
target_overlap: ROCmFPX's cache is run-scoped.
rationale: Use the same versioned persistent manifest and atomic commit layer as conversation checkpoints.
risks: Startup memory cost scales with stored system entries because state blobs are loaded into RAM.

behavior: Expires system cache entries after a configured unused-day limit and evicts LRU entries above a maximum count.
dependencies: wall clock | LRU metadata | filesystem delete
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has byte-bounded LRU mechanics.
rationale: Combine age, byte, and count limits; expose tenant and global quotas.
risks: Wall-clock changes and large state variance require conservative accounting.

feature: Full-prompt hash plus bounded token prefix
behavior: Keys a system entry by a full prompt hash and records a bounded token prefix and compatibility metadata.
dependencies: stable tokenization | hash function | compatibility fingerprint
target_overlap: ROCmFPX can reuse its token vectors and target/draft validation.
rationale: Use a cryptographic or collision-resistant content key over canonical tokens and include template/model/tenant scope.
risks: Hash collisions or tokenization drift must fail closed.

behavior: Decodes token text and searches for user/human/end-of-generation markers to decide where the reusable system prefix ends.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX supports multiple chat templates and structured request conversion.
rationale: Derive the boundary from the parsed message/template AST before tokenization, then verify the exact token range.
risks: Heuristics can cache user content as a shared system prefix.

behavior: Compares incoming tokens with stored checkpoint prefixes and ranks by longest common prefix, recency, and checkpoint length.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already performs LCP matching for RAM and disk prompt cache entries.
rationale: Consolidate around the target implementation and add restart-persistent index candidates.
risks: Minimum acceptance and exact state boundary rules must remain caller-specific.

behavior: Requires approximately 90% token-prefix similarity before restoring another conversation's checkpoint.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX prompt caching already matches prefixes within the running server.
rationale: Make threshold configurable by scope; require authenticated tenant equality and a minimum absolute token count.
risks: A ratio alone is unsafe for short prompts.

behavior: Searches anonymous cache directories for a stored prompt that can continue a new conversation.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX does not retain cross-run directories.
rationale: Replace global scanning with a manifest/index partitioned by model and authenticated tenant; anonymous reuse should default to process-local only.
risks: Cross-user data reuse and unbounded I/O.

behavior: Rejects very small continuation comparisons before treating them as a useful session match.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX can apply this in its candidate filter.
rationale: Use both minimum absolute tokens and ratio thresholds, with higher requirements for cross-conversation or cross-restart matches.
risks: Fixed thresholds may be model/template dependent.

behavior: Uses a configurable slot-prompt similarity threshold to choose a warm slot with a reusable prefix.
license: MIT for component; GPL-3.0 for parent profile
target_overlap: ROCmFPX inherits llama.cpp slot prompt reuse.
rationale: Keep target behavior; document interaction with persistent cache and user affinity.
risks: Affinity and prefix reuse must be evaluated under one authorization-aware selection policy.

behavior: Prefetches the selected checkpoint so restore latency can overlap request preparation.
target_overlap: No target equivalent was identified.
rationale: Add only after persistence and candidate correctness are tested; instrument useful-prefetch ratio.
risks: Can amplify SSD writes/reads and page-cache churn.

behavior: Creates checkpoints at configured token intervals while processing long prompts.
dependencies: llama sequence state API | checkpoint interval | prompt token progress
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has context checkpoint controls and prompt-cache saves.
rationale: Keep target checkpoint scheduling and integrate persistent snapshots as a separate policy.
risks: Source and documentation disagree on the minimum/default step; very frequent snapshots can dominate I/O.

behavior: Marks a final checkpoint for creation after the first generated token so the restored state has the needed generation boundary.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has prompt-cache saves at task boundaries.
rationale: Preserve the semantic boundary, but express it as an explicit checkpoint reason/state in the target.
risks: Ordering bugs can persist a state that cannot resume generation correctly.

behavior: Restores target state, optional draft state, and speculative state into a selected slot.
dependencies: llama_state_seq_set_data_ext | draft context | spec state decoder
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already stores target/draft and stateful MTP records.
rationale: Merge semantics into the target's paired-state validation and exact-boundary rules.
risks: A draft/spec mismatch must force safe catch-up or full prefill.

behavior: Loads a serialized sequence into the currently assigned server slot rather than assuming the source slot ID.
dependencies: extended sequence state API | destination slot
target_overlap: The target uses per-slot sequence state APIs.
rationale: Keep explicit destination sequence IDs in every restore API and add a regression test based on the historical cold-restore fix.
risks: Implicit source IDs can restore into the wrong sequence.

behavior: Clears attention KV state while preserving recurrent state for hybrid/recurrent models.
dependencies: hybrid memory implementation | model architecture detection
target_overlap: ROCmFPX includes MTP and evolving recurrent/hybrid support.
rationale: Retain the primitive only if the target base does not already contain an equivalent; validate per architecture.
risks: Incorrect partial clearing can silently corrupt recurrent continuation.

behavior: Exposes named slot-state files through an HTTP action route when a slot-save path is configured.
dependencies: slot save directory | filename validation | HTTP server
target_overlap: ROCmFPX inherits the slot-state API family.
rationale: Keep the endpoint but enforce owner-only directories, API authorization, quotas, and audit logs.
risks: Named files are an administrative surface separate from automatic cache persistence.

behavior: Treats failed or incomplete restores as misses and continues through normal prompt processing.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX tests corruption and partial target/draft pairs.
rationale: Use the target's stricter file-size/pair validation and circuit-breaker semantics.
risks: Fallback must clear any partially applied sequence state.

behavior: Maintains reusable prompt states in RAM in addition to SSD-backed checkpoints.
dependencies: host RAM budget | server prompt cache
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has a byte-bounded RAM prompt cache.
rationale: Keep the target implementation as the first tier; persistent disk should be a lower tier.
risks: RAM accounting must include target, draft, and metadata.

behavior: Can reuse sufficiently large prompt chunks via KV shifting under the server cache-reuse setting.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already documents and carries cache-reuse behavior.
rationale: Retain target-native behavior; test interactions with loaded persistent state and hybrid memory.
risks: Not all memory types support arbitrary shifting.

behavior: Accepts llama_user_id in OpenAI-style request bodies and propagates it to task scheduling.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has OpenAI-compatible endpoints but no verified authenticated tenant cache scope.
rationale: Accept a user hint only behind a trusted gateway; bind an internal tenant principal from API-key/JWT context.
risks: Client-supplied identity is spoofable.

behavior: Maps metadata.user_id from Anthropic-style requests into the same scheduling identity field.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX may retain Anthropic compatibility from its llama.cpp base.
rationale: Keep protocol parsing as a hint, then map through the same authenticated principal layer as OpenAI requests.
risks: Protocol parity must not create different authorization rules.

behavior: Validates length and allowed characters before using an identifier in scheduling or filesystem namespace selection.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX should validate any external label before logging or lookup.
rationale: Retain strict syntax validation but store a keyed hash/opaque internal ID instead of the raw value.
risks: Validation prevents traversal but not identity spoofing.

behavior: Rejects or defers requests when a non-empty user identity reaches the configured in-flight limit.
dependencies: active-user counter | server slots | HTTP admission
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has global slot limits but no assessed tenant quota.
rationale: Implement one authoritative scheduler quota keyed by authenticated tenant, with atomic admission and release.
risks: Pinned code duplicates checks at HTTP and allocator layers; races and accounting drift are possible.

behavior: Documentation describes a shared anonymous bucket, but the pinned code explicitly exempts empty user IDs from per-user accounting.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX should not inherit the contradiction.
rationale: Define an explicit unauthenticated/global policy; production multi-tenant deployments should require authentication.
risks: Anonymous traffic can consume all global slots.

behavior: Prefers a least-recently-used slot previously associated with the same user to improve reuse.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already chooses slots using prompt similarity and availability.
rationale: Combine authorization, user affinity, and prefix score in a single eligibility/ranking pass; never select cross-tenant state.
risks: Separate selection passes can accidentally prioritize prefix reuse before isolation.

behavior: Creates persistent cache wrappers and paths under a user namespace.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has private process directories, not persistent tenant namespaces.
rationale: Namespace by authenticated tenant hash and model fingerprint, with per-tenant owner/key policy.
risks: Raw IDs in paths leak identity and allow spoofed cache access.

behavior: The architecture has user cache maps, but pinned get_stats aggregation omits them.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has cache counters but no assessed per-tenant view.
rationale: Do not port the omission; define aggregate and tenant-scoped metrics with cardinality controls.
risks: Operational dashboards would underreport persistent usage.

feature: Per-user tier aging on turn completion
behavior: The pinned turn-completion path advances anonymous caches but omits user cache wrappers.
target_overlap: No direct target equivalent.
rationale: Centralize all cache instances in one registry and iterate one lifecycle interface.
risks: User entries can remain hot indefinitely or avoid intended eviction.

behavior: Logs scheduling/rate-limit decisions with the unredacted user identifier.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX logs are shared operational output.
rationale: Log a stable keyed pseudonym, not raw identity; keep raw values out of metrics labels.
risks: PII/secrets leakage and high-cardinality observability.

feature: Identity as routing metadata, not authentication
behavior: The user identifier is accepted from the request body and is not itself a credential or verified principal.
dependencies: API key/TLS optionally elsewhere | request metadata
target_overlap: ROCmFPX supports API keys/TLS but needs explicit identity binding.
rationale: Resolve tenant identity in authenticated middleware and ignore/validate client hints according to gateway policy.
risks: Using body metadata as a security boundary enables cache theft.

feature: Unified cache and slot ownership lifecycle
behavior: Ownership state is currently distributed across task parsing, slot counters, slot user fields, and separate page-manager maps.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has its own scheduler and cache engine.
rationale: Introduce one TenantContext/CacheScope object passed through admission, selection, restore, save, metrics, and release.
risks: Distributed accounting is difficult to audit and test.

feature: SSD cache CLI and environment controls
behavior: Exposes path, tier windows/budgets, checkpoint limits, system-prompt limits, retention, fsync, and concurrency settings.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX currently exposes --cache-disk and --cache-disk-limit.
rationale: Extend target-native naming with explicit persistent-mode, durability, retention, and namespace controls; preserve backward compatibility.
risks: Cachy source, docs, and parent runner use conflicting defaults.

behavior: llama-ai supplies operational defaults that differ from component defaults and selects cache use by model/hardware profile.
dependencies: shell environment | model metadata probe | hardware detector
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has build/run scripts but should not directly import GPL shell code into its MIT tree.
rationale: Re-express useful profile rules in an MIT-compatible configuration layer or external GPL deployment project.
risks: License incompatibility for direct incorporation; default drift.

behavior: Prunes cache entries not used within a configured number of days.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX currently evicts by byte pressure and run lifetime.
rationale: Add optional age eviction to persistent mode with monotonic/validated timestamps and dry-run reporting.
risks: Clock rollback and unreadable metadata.

behavior: Deletes an old conversation cache directory when the configured conversation limit is reached.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX uses byte-bounded LRU entries.
rationale: Use manifest-backed LRU/bytes per tenant; do not choose victims solely by directory mtime.
risks: Separate user/anonymous limits and non-atomic deletion.

behavior: Discovers existing persistent entries at startup; malformed or expired entries can be skipped or removed.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already cleans stale private run directories using ownership markers and locks.
rationale: Combine target ownership/lock safety with a persistent manifest, quarantine, bounded reconciliation, and schema migration.
risks: Concurrent instances and partial entries need clear ownership.

behavior: No dedicated HTTP endpoint for listing, inspecting, pruning, or invalidating automatic SSD cache entries was identified.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX likewise exposes metrics/slots rather than a persistent-cache admin API.
rationale: Add authenticated inspect/prune/invalidate endpoints or an offline admin CLI, with tenant scoping and dry-run.
risks: Administrative APIs can expose prompt metadata and become a destructive control surface.

behavior: Cache internals track hits, misses, bytes, tiers, and restore timing, but complete user-scoped aggregation is not wired into the standard metrics endpoint.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already tracks disk saves, loads, evictions, failures, and prompt cache hits in logs/timings.
rationale: Expose low-cardinality cache counters and gauges from one target cache engine.
risks: Metrics cardinality and undercounting.

behavior: Compatibility checks cause old state to be rejected when model/cache identity changes.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX model formats and MTP state evolve rapidly.
rationale: Retain fail-closed rejection and add explicit invalidate/migrate tooling keyed by exact model fingerprint.
risks: Rejected files can consume disk indefinitely without cleanup.

behavior: A second hot/warm/cold page-manager implementation includes asynchronous writeback concepts but is not linked into the active common library.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already has a working prompt cache engine.
rationale: Do not port this duplicate path. Extract only independently valuable test ideas after verifying semantics.
risks: Unbuilt code, inconsistent size comments/literals, duplicate architecture.

behavior: Runs each loaded model in a child llama-server process behind a router and proxies requests to the selected child.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX inherits modern llama.cpp router capabilities or can reconcile against them.
rationale: Retain upstream/target router implementation rather than transplanting an older fork copy.
risks: Router mode is explicitly experimental and unsuitable for untrusted direct exposure.

behavior: Exposes explicit model load and unload operations through JSON endpoints.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX's current base may already contain equivalent model routes.
rationale: Use target-native routes and apply authentication, authorization, resource quotas, and audit logging.
risks: Loading arbitrary presets can execute resource-heavy or unsafe configurations.

feature: Model autoload on first routed request
behavior: Optionally starts an unloaded configured model when a request names it.
dependencies: model catalog | child process manager | HTTP proxy
target_overlap: ROCmFPX documents model router controls in its inherited server.
rationale: Retain behind an explicit policy and admission controller.
risks: Cold-start latency and denial-of-service by model thrashing.

feature: Maximum loaded-model count with LRU unload
behavior: Caps active child models and unloads the least recently used model before loading another.
target_overlap: Applicable to ROCmFPX where large quantized models compete for UMA/VRAM.
rationale: Retain target-native LRU but make memory pressure and pinned models first-class inputs.
risks: Request-level recency alone may evict an expensive or pinned model.

behavior: Reloads model definitions, updates metadata, autoloads newly configured models, and broadcasts a lifecycle event.
target_overlap: Useful for ROCmFPX model presets and quant variants.
rationale: Retain with schema validation and atomic catalog swap.
risks: Partial reloads and stale child parameters.

behavior: Loads model presets from cache, a configured models directory, and preset sources.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX users manage many quantized variants.
rationale: Keep target-native discovery with explicit trust boundaries and allowlisted roots.
risks: Untrusted presets and path traversal.

feature: Hugging Face GGUF discovery and split download
behavior: The parent launcher resolves repository files and downloads complete or split GGUF artifacts using available Hugging Face tools.
dependencies: hf CLI or huggingface_hub | network | disk space
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has its own distribution/build workflows.
rationale: Implement or document an MIT-compatible downloader outside the inference core; verify checksums and free space.
risks: Directly copying parent shell code would import GPL obligations; remote artifacts are untrusted input.

behavior: The parent inspects GGUF metadata to choose dense, MoE, recurrent/SSM, and hardware-specific launch profiles.
dependencies: GGUF metadata | shell parsing | hardware profile
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has multiple quant families, backends, MTP paths, and Strix profiles.
rationale: Reimplement as a declarative, tested preset resolver in the target or an external deployment package.
risks: Heuristic metadata scanning from the first file bytes is brittle.

feature: Cache scope tied to model compatibility
behavior: Persistent states are accepted only for a compatible model/cache fingerprint, naturally invalidating reuse after incompatible model changes.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX frequently changes quant type and MTP layout.
rationale: Namespace cache roots by exact model fingerprint and runtime state ABI, not just human model alias.
risks: Aliases can point to different files over time.

behavior: Serves OpenAI-compatible chat-completions and completions endpoints, including streaming.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX is built on a newer llama.cpp server.
rationale: Keep target-native API behavior and add cache/user extensions through namespaced fields or headers.
risks: Compatibility fields evolve; avoid fork-only semantics without versioning.

behavior: Converts Responses API requests to chat-completion internals and emits Responses-style events.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX's target base already includes modern response formatting.
rationale: Reconcile with target rather than cherry-picking fork code.

behavior: Converts Anthropic Messages requests to internal chat completions and returns Anthropic-formatted streaming/non-streaming responses.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX may already carry this upstream surface.
rationale: Retain target-native implementation; map metadata.user_id only through trusted identity policy.

behavior: Exposes native completion and fill-in-the-middle operations in addition to OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
target_overlap: Useful for coding models quantized by ROCmFPX.
rationale: Keep target-native support and capability checks.

behavior: Supports embedding generation and rank-model reranking when the server is started in the corresponding mode.
target_overlap: Independent of cache port and likely already present in target.

behavior: Maps supported audio transcription requests through multimodal chat processing.

behavior: Provides GET slot status and POST save/restore/erase operations for a selected slot.
target_overlap: Likely inherited by ROCmFPX.
rationale: Keep with authentication and distinguish manual slot files from automatic persistent cache entries.

behavior: Associates SSE output with a conversation ID and exposes lookup, retrieval, and deletion for reconnecting clients.

target_overlap: ROCmFPX can benefit for long agent outputs independently of KV persistence.

behavior: Lists configured models, reports status/presets, loads/unloads models, and streams lifecycle events.
dependencies: router mode | SSE | child process manager
target_overlap: Useful for ROCmFPX quant variants.
rationale: Use target-native router API with authorization and resource controls.
risks: Experimental surface and sensitive preset exposure.

behavior: Lists and changes active LoRA adapters without a process restart.
target_overlap: Useful to ROCmFPX models and independent of cache implementation.
rationale: Keep target-native implementation; include adapter set in cache compatibility fingerprint.

behavior: Registers expert tracking/statistics and control routes for MoE diagnostics and tuning.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has strong MoE/Strix interest but target instrumentation may differ.
rationale: Treat as an optional diagnostic extension; reconcile against target graph/kernel architecture and protect control endpoints.

behavior: Exposes tokenizer conversion and chat-template rendering without running inference.
target_overlap: Useful for exact persistent-cache key construction and clients.

behavior: Reports health during load/sleep and exposes model/server capability metadata.

behavior: Emits prompt/generation counters, throughput, request queue depth, slot utilization, and process start time.

behavior: Returns cached prompt-token counts and prompt/generation timing in completion results.

behavior: Logs checkpoint saves, restores, evictions, cold starts, and failures.

behavior: Broadcasts model load, unload, and reload events to connected clients.
target_overlap: Useful for orchestration around large ROCmFPX models.

behavior: Exposes expert-selection information for MoE analysis.

behavior: Internal cache statistics exist, but pinned server aggregation omits user cache maps.

behavior: Builds CachyLlama for Vulkan, ROCm/HIP, or Metal with backend-specific CMake settings.
dependencies: CMake | compiler toolchain | Vulkan SDK or ROCm or Metal

behavior: Runs llama-server as a managed service with restart policy and hardening directives.

behavior: Force-kills existing llama-server processes and port holders before starting a new server.
dependencies: pkill | fuser/lsof or process inspection | shell privileges

behavior: Supports API-key authentication and server TLS certificate/key options.
dependencies: TLS library/backend | HTTP middleware | secret storage

rationale: Keep target-native implementation and use authenticated principal context for cache tenant binding.

behavior: Selects local models or downloads Hugging Face GGUF files before launch.

behavior: Maps AMD PCI/device information to gfx targets, HSA overrides, memory tiers, and recommended profiles.

risks: Device IDs and driver behavior evolve.

behavior: Can use amd-smi or mutate systemd-boot/GRUB kernel parameters to expand GPU-accessible memory.

behavior: Component source defaults, server documentation, and parent profile overrides form three configuration layers.

behavior: The inference component is MIT, while the parent launch/build/deployment layer is GPL-3.0 and its documentation has a separate content license.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX is MIT.
rationale: Port MIT component code with notices; clean-room reimplement parent behavior or keep it as a separate GPL work.

behavior: Recognizes Strix Halo gfx1151 in deployment and HIP architecture classification.

target_overlap: ROCmFPX explicitly targets Strix Halo and already carries RDNA3.5 support.

risks: Hard-coded HSA overrides can hide real compiler/runtime incompatibility.

behavior: Exports an HSA gfx override and unified-memory settings for Strix Halo ROCm execution.

rationale: Keep target-documented environment and add version-gated validation rather than copying shell code.
risks: Overrides vary by ROCm release.

behavior: Chooses large contexts and may disable SSD checkpointing for selected dense/MoE Halo profiles because UMA can hold state in memory.

rationale: Convert to a declarative memory estimator based on model/KV/context/parallelism, retaining SSD as an explicit resilience option.
risks: Static profiles can exceed memory or disable useful restart persistence.

behavior: Uses RDNA3.5-specific warp choices for quantized matrix-vector generation paths.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has newer custom ROCmFPX kernel formats and target-specific tuning.
rationale: Benchmark-port individual launch heuristics per ROCmFPX type; do not wholesale replace target kernels.
risks: Tuning for Q/K/IQ types may not transfer to ROCmFPX formats.

behavior: Selects a larger warp count for a narrow recurrent gated-delta-net shape on RDNA3.5.

rationale: Cherry-pick concept only after target-side correctness and end-to-end model benchmarks.
risks: Shape-specific tuning can regress other models.

behavior: Classifies AMD Vulkan devices using subgroup and integer-dot capabilities to select architecture-specific paths.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX recommends Vulkan for several tested Strix decode workloads and has newer Vulkan kernels.
rationale: Keep target-native implementation; reconcile any missing capability logic narrowly.
risks: Capability inference can conflate RDNA generations.

behavior: Counts all memory heaps for integrated GPUs rather than only device-local heaps when reporting capacity.
dependencies: VK_EXT_memory_budget when available | integrated GPU detection
target_overlap: Directly relevant to Strix Halo UMA and likely present in the newer target.
rationale: Retain target implementation and add pressure-aware reservations rather than treating all UMA as available.
risks: Reported budget is not equivalent to safe allocatable memory.

feature: Vulkan graph reordering and fusion preservation
behavior: Reorders graph nodes around MoE, normalization, recurrent, and view patterns to improve execution while preserving dependencies.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX has a newer Vulkan backend with ROCmFPX-specific shaders.
rationale: Diff at symbol level and port only missing optimizer cases with backend-op correctness tests.
risks: Large backend files have high merge-conflict and regression risk.

behavior: Records exact environment, canary models, correctness totals, benchmark commands, and rejected kernel experiments.
target_overlap: ROCmFPX already publishes Strix/MTP benchmarks and experimental status.
rationale: Retain the engineering practice: every kernel change needs correctness gates, matched baselines, and a rejection record.
risks: Notes mix clean commits and dirty local builds; provenance must be normalized.

behavior: Local evidence favors Vulkan over HIP for selected Strix Halo decode workloads, while both backends are supported.

behavior: Prioritizes MoE throughput and uses Qwen/GPT-OSS canaries while accepting some dense-model tradeoffs when correctness is intact.

rationale: Separate kernel/profile presets by workload rather than one global Strix default.
risks: A MoE-biased default can regress dense models.

behavior: ROCmFPX already spills prompt state to a private, byte-bounded disk namespace for the current server run.
dependencies: llama state file API | filesystem | prompt cache
target_overlap: This is the target implementation.
rationale: Keep as the default non-persistent mode and extend rather than replace it.
risks: Not reusable after clean restart by design.

behavior: Writes target and optional draft state through temporary files, validates size, flushes, renames atomically, and syncs the directory.
target_overlap: This is the strongest persistence primitive in the target.
rationale: Use it as the foundation for persistent CachyLlama-style checkpoints.
risks: Manifest publication must be made equally atomic.

behavior: Disables further disk saves after an I/O failure while preserving safe fallback behavior and accounting.
target_overlap: This is the target implementation.
rationale: Preserve for persistent mode and expose breaker state in metrics/health.
risks: A permanent breaker may require an administrative reset or retry policy.

behavior: Tests hits, LRU, target/draft pairs, corruption, failure handling, cleanup, and accounting.
target_overlap: This is target validation infrastructure.
rationale: Extend it with restart persistence, manifest corruption, tenant isolation, concurrent instances, and upgrade tests.
risks: Hardware-independent tests do not replace live ROCm/Vulkan validation.

behavior: Treats stateful MTP cache records as exact-token-boundary entries while allowing ordinary stateless prefixes to subsume shorter entries.
target_overlap: This is target behavior.
rationale: Preserve when adding persistence and system-prefix caching.
risks: Relaxing exact-boundary rules can restore invalid speculative state.

feature: Strix Halo ROCmFPX and MTP baseline
behavior: Already supplies Strix Halo build scripts, HIP/Vulkan paths, ROCmFPX quants, MTP execution, and published local validation.
target_overlap: This is the target baseline.
rationale: Port server/cache capabilities without overwriting newer quant/backend/MTP work.
risks: The target is explicitly experimental and performance is workload-specific.

behavior: Can expose read, search, write, edit, diff, time, and shell-execution tools through /tools.

target_overlap: ROCmFPX is an inference/quant target and should not couple privileged host tools to its public model server.
rationale: Keep disabled; place tools in a separately sandboxed, authenticated agent runtime if needed.
risks: Remote code execution and filesystem disclosure.

behavior: Can expose a Web UI CORS proxy for MCP integrations.

risks: SSRF, credential forwarding, and trust-boundary collapse.

behavior: Registers compatibility handling for Google Cloud Platform serving conventions.
target_overlap: May already exist in the target's newer llama.cpp server.
rationale: Retain target-native implementation if required by deployments.
risks: Compatibility surface requires upstream conformance tests.

behavior: Can put the server into a sleep state after a configured idle interval while preserving health access.
target_overlap: Useful for large UMA models sharing a workstation.
rationale: Keep target-native behavior; define how persistent caches and router children behave across sleep/wake.
risks: Wake latency and stale device state.

behavior: Can estimate device requirements and adjust unset launch parameters, including context and offload, toward a target memory margin.
